speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; could you tell me when these gait and limb coordination problems first started and if they've been getting worse over time? Have you noticed any other symptoms like vision changes, muscle weakness, or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, so the symptoms are progressive and predominantly affect your right side; have you experienced any recent headaches, nausea, or changes in your vision? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent use of natalizumab, have you experienced any severe headaches, visual disturbances, or cognitive changes? I am also going to request a brain MRI to look for signs of demyelination. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature Normothermic, Blood Pressure Within normal range, Heart Rate Within normal range, Respiratory Rate Within normal range. Neurological Examination: Gait Assessment shows ataxic gait; Right Upper Limb Strength is 4/5; Coordination Tests show evidence of ataxia. MRI Brain: Findings indicate lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML); T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions combined with your recent natalizumab use strongly suggest Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Do you recall experiencing any new cognitive changes or personality shifts alongside your physical symptoms?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
